findings.obligation: The acceptance designer owns every test; the implementation author adds a test only where the recorded oracle cannot go green without it, and never beyond the recorded oracle (nw-code-craftsmanship rule 35; nw-sc-review-dimensions, Producer-Authored Tests). acceptance.md records every oracle locator, in-crate ones included.
findings.observation: Open, and the remedy is now demonstrated by the project itself. Both proptests remain outside the recorded oracle: acceptance.md at HEAD 5843ed2 records fourteen locators, eight journeys and three properties in tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs, two check-arch entries, and three in-crate ones in crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs (a_purge_between_scan_start_and_plan_write_leaves_no_rows at line 180, a_run_saves_its_first_mark_and_is_refused_the_next at 389, the_run_after_it_saves_its_own_first_mark at 418); neither of these two is among them. This delta shows the acceptance designer recording in-crate adapter tests as oracle locators when they belong to the oracle, which is exactly the disposition these two still lack. The oracle also now covers L1 broadly and records the L4 cases, so neither proptest is the sole cover of anything. The oracle goes green without them: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture exited 0 with 11 passed, neither among them. Nothing is weakened and no behaviour is affected.
findings.remediation: Either remove both, whose obligations acceptance.md now records against oracle locators, or have the acceptance designer record them in acceptance.md the way a_run_saves_its_first_mark_and_is_refused_the_next was recorded, so every test in the candidate has one owner. Raise a future gap to the acceptance designer rather than closing it in a production crate.

findings.obligation: A rule the code checks at runtime, or only in a test, that the types could make impossible is a finding (nw-type-level-design, 'Decide before writing' 4 and 'Write' 3; nw-certainty-by-construction).
findings.observation: Open and unchanged by the delta; retained as non-blocking. Resume still models a four-way partition of the plan's positions as four parallel public collections, to_read, carried, already_read and skipped, the fourth added by this feature. Nothing in the type stops one position appearing in two of them; the disjointness the count depends on is asserted only by property tests. Resume::kept at resume.rs:104-125 already rebuilds the per-position-with-disposition sequence the type could carry, and the revised oracle binding now consumes exactly that sequence (sut_picked_up reads verdict.kept()), so the shape the type is missing is the one the oracle already reads. The owner states that reshaping Resume would disturb that binding; the remediation below keeps kept(), to_read, carried, already_read and skipped as public observations, so the binding and tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs:402 are unaffected.
findings.remediation: Carry the verdict as one sequence of positions each with its disposition - the KeptRow shape already introduced, extended with the carried-skip reason - and derive to_read, carried, already_read, skipped and kept() over it, so no two of them can name the same position and every current reader keeps its surface. Not required for this feature; schedule it with the next change to the resume verdict.

findings.location: docs/feature/fix-repos-read-across-resume/architecture.md, the declared verification commands of slice S1, command 6
findings.obligation: A declared verification command is authority the crafter and every reviewer must be able to run; a command in a README, runbook or design that cannot run as written is a defect in the artifact that states it (nw-code-craftsmanship 39; the design owns the verification commands it declares).
findings.observation: argv: cargo test -p openlore-review-app --lib. exit 101. stderr: 'error: no library targets found in package openlore-review-app'. The package declares bins and integration test targets and no lib target, so the command can never pass; the crafter substituted cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins, which I ran at exit 0 with 39 passed. The substitution is right but undeclared, so the next reader of the design runs a command that fails and cannot tell an authority typo from a real regression.
findings.remediation: Correct command 6 of the S1 verification commands to cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins, the target that actually holds the in-crate tests of config.rs and wiring.rs, and keep the rest of the list as it is.

findings.location: crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs:304, 391, 424-432 and 610-612 (the scan_write field, ScanWriteSeam and admits_scan_write)
findings.obligation: Avoid work on a hot path that no accepted outcome needs, and add no element a release build cannot use (nw-code-craftsmanship 33; nw-code-design-oo 'Decide before writing' 7). Every refusal or failure path you add gets one assertion that fails on a constructed violation (nw-code-craftsmanship 36).
findings.observation: The test-only seam now costs a release build a lock and a new failure mode on the path of every saved read. ReviewStore::scan_write changed from a Copy Option<ScanWriteFault> read without synchronisation to Mutex<ScanWriteSeam>, and admits_scan_write takes that lock on every mark_repo_read. In a release build ScanWriteFault is uninhabited (lib.rs:571-573), so the seam can refuse nothing there by construction, yet the lock is still acquired and admits_scan_write can now return StoreError::Database('scan write seam lock poisoned'), a production error path that did not exist before and that no test observes. The struct's own comment, 'a production store carries no seam state at all', is true of the set's contents but not of the Mutex or of that error path. The extra lock is small beside the DuckDB transaction it precedes, so this is a cleanliness and honesty finding, not a measured performance one; I make no timing claim.
findings.remediation: Gate the seam itself on #[cfg(debug_assertions)]: keep ReviewStore::scan_write as the plain Option<ScanWriteFault> it was in a release build and call the pure admits directly, so the release path has no lock and no poisoned-lock branch, and let the development build hold Mutex<ScanWriteSeam>. The uninhabited ScanWriteFault already makes the release refusal unrepresentable, so no behaviour is lost. If the single shape is kept deliberately, correct the comment to say what the release build does carry.

findings.location: The mutation evidence for crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs admits, reported as 8 of 9 viable mutants caught
findings.obligation: Required verification evidence that is missing, unrun or inconclusive is a finding; a mutant recorded as missed must be measured against the tests that can kill it, not against a selection that cannot (the project's declared per-feature mutation gate, kill rate at or above 80 per cent, scoped to modified files).
findings.observation: The one recorded miss deletes the admits arm of the two pre-existing faults, and the crafter states it was not measured against review_app_scan_store_failure. That suite is a recorded oracle locator, it drives exactly those two tokens at tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:57-62 and asserts the run ends 'interrupted' at line 156, so deleting the arm would fail it; crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:693-707 pins the same tokens independently. The mutant is therefore unmeasured rather than surviving, by reading those two test bodies, and the declared 80 per cent gate is met at 8 of 9 either way. What is missing is the measurement: as recorded, the evidence reads as a surviving mutant in the fault seam, and a later reader cannot tell that from a real gap.
findings.remediation: Re-run the mutation measurement for crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs with review_app_scan_store_failure in the test selection, or record beside the result that this mutant's killing test lives in the openlore-review-app acceptance targets and is outside the adapter-scoped run, naming the two locators above. I could not measure it myself: constructing the mutant means editing candidate production bytes, which this role may not do.

observations.text: Third correction re-review. HEAD is now 5843ed2, tree clean; argv: git status --porcelain -> exit 0, stdout empty. argv: git diff --stat 3ab2dd1 HEAD -> exit 0: production changed this time. crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs (+120/-), crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs, crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs (+6), crates/openlore-review-app/src/wiring.rs (+4), xtask/src/check_arch.rs (+7), the new xtask/tests/review_app_test_fault_guard.rs (+56), the oracle file (+207), the two acceptance support files (+24), and the feature docs and run records. crates/review-domain and crates/ports are byte-identical to the revision R4 observed. Affected and re-executed: the S1 oracle suite, adapter-review-store with review-domain and ports, xtask, the architectural check, clippy over the three touched packages with --all-targets, the review-app bins, and the whole openlore-review-app package.

Affected checks re-executed at HEAD 5843ed2, each argv with its exit and result. (1) cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume -- --nocapture: exit 0, 11 passed 0 failed, two more than the 9 of R17, exactly a_new_scan_accounts_for_its_own_repos_only and a_run_cut_short_after_saving_a_read_of_its_own_keeps_it_for_the_run_after_it. (2) cargo test -p adapter-review-store -p review-domain -p ports: exit 0, 265 passed 0 failed over 11 binaries, two more than the 263 of R4, exactly a_run_saves_its_first_mark_and_is_refused_the_next and the_run_after_it_saves_its_own_first_mark. (3) cargo test -p xtask: exit 0, 380 passed 0 failed over 20 binaries, including the seven of the new review_app_test_fault_guard.rs. (4) cargo xtask check-arch: exit 0, 'check-arch: OK (30 workspace members)'. (5) cargo clippy -p adapter-review-store -p openlore-review-app -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings: exit 0, no warning. (6) cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins: exit 0, 39 passed 0 failed, which is where the config.rs fault-token property runs. (7) cargo test -p openlore-review-app: exit 0, 322 passed 0 failed over 22 binaries, every binary 'test result: ok', review_app_scan_store_failure among them.

The reported missed mutant is unmeasured, not surviving, and its killing test is a recorded oracle locator. The miss deletes the arm of crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs admits that reads (Some(RefuseMarkRepoRead), MarkRepoRead{..}) | (Some(RefuseRecordAccountChecks), RecordAccountChecks) => Err(ScanWriteRefused). tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:57-62 drives exactly those two tokens, 'refuse_mark_repo_read' and 'refuse_record_account_checks', through the real binary's REVIEW_APP_TEST_FAULT seam, and then_the_scan_ended_interrupted at line 156 asserts the run ends 'interrupted'. With that arm deleted neither write is refused, both scans complete, and that assertion fails, so the suite kills the mutant; a cargo-mutants run scoped to the adapter crate does not run a review-app acceptance target, which is why it was recorded as a miss. Independently, crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs:693-707 pins each of the four fault tokens to its variant in a development build, so a mutant deleting a test_fault arm is killed there too, under cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins. I did not construct the mutant myself: doing so would mean editing candidate production bytes, which this role may not do, so the kill above is a reasoned judgement from the two cited test bodies and not a measured one. The project's declared gate is a kill rate of at least 80 per cent and the crafter measured 8 of 9, which meets it even if the miss were counted as surviving.

The new production seam is correct and its guard is exemplary. ScanWrite::MarkRepoRead now carries run_id, which crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs:281 supplies from the argument it already holds, so no caller learns anything new; the decision stays in the pure total admits, now also given whether that run already saved a mark, and the seam's bookkeeping (ScanWriteSeam::answer, saved_a_mark, remember) is the only mutable part. remember inserts only when a fault is held, so a production store accumulates no run ids. ScanWriteFault is uninhabited under #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] (lib.rs:571-573) and the release twin of admits still matches on the empty type, so a release build can refuse nothing by construction. xtask/src/check_arch.rs adds both new tokens to REVIEW_APP_TEST_FAULT_TOKENS, and the new xtask/tests/review_app_test_fault_guard.rs exercises the guard against a temp workspace with a positive control, a negative control per touched file, the store-variant pair and the real tree, so the guard itself is falsifiable rather than asserted. The two new in-crate adapter tests are recorded oracle locators in acceptance.md at lines 389 and 418, so they are the acceptance designer's and not producer-authored strays; the xtask guard test is an architectural test, which the producer owns, under the check-arch obligation acceptance.md already records at line 360.

The two new journeys discriminate what nothing before them could. a_new_scan_accounts_for_its_own_repos_only observes E4 through the real HTTP port: she scans three repos, unticks one and scans again, and the queue must say two, not the five her two scans read between them; a scan-chain count would say five, so the journey fails on the alternative the ADR rejected. a_run_cut_short_after_saving_a_read_of_its_own_keeps_it_for_the_run_after_it is the reason the new fault exists: it builds the one state in which a whole-scan count and a last-run count differ while the last run reads strictly less, asserts that the cut-short run ends 'interrupted' and shows NO repos-read line at all, that the run picking it up read strictly fewer repos than the whole scan and not nothing, and that the queue then says two. then_her_scan_read_the_repos_she_chose was generalised to take the chosen set as a parameter rather than hard-coding PRIYA_CHOICE_OF_THREE, which widens it to the two-repo journeys without weakening it; every expected value in both journeys is still anchored to her saved choice and to the repos the GitHub double was asked for, never to production output.

diagnostic: Accepted at HEAD 5843ed2. The new production seam is correct and well guarded, both new journeys discriminate behaviour nothing before them could, every affected check is green, and the one declared command that fails is an authority typo rather than a regression. Five findings stay open, all non-blocking: one owner design, four owner implementation. Re-executed at HEAD, each with its argv: the S1 oracle suite, exit 0, 11 passed, two more than before and exactly the two new journeys; adapter-review-store with review-domain and ports, exit 0, 265 passed over 11 binaries, two more and exactly the two new in-crate adapter tests; xtask, exit 0, 380 passed over 20 binaries including the seven of the new fault guard; cargo xtask check-arch, exit 0, OK over 30 workspace members; clippy over adapter-review-store, openlore-review-app and xtask with --all-targets and -D warnings, exit 0, no warning; cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins, exit 0, 39 passed; the whole openlore-review-app package, exit 0, 322 passed over 22 binaries with review_app_scan_store_failure among them. crates/review-domain and crates/ports are byte-identical to the revision R4 observed, so that run was not repeated. On the production delta: ScanWrite::MarkRepoRead carries the run id the adapter already held at the call site, the decision stays in the pure total admits, the seam's bookkeeping remembers a run only while a fault is held, ScanWriteFault is uninhabited in a release build so nothing can be refused there by construction, and the new xtask guard test exercises the check against a temp workspace with positive and negative controls and the real tree, which makes the guard falsifiable rather than asserted. The two new in-crate adapter tests are recorded oracle locators in acceptance.md at lines 389 and 418, so they are the acceptance designer's, and the xtask guard is an architectural test the producer owns under the check-arch obligation recorded at line 360. The two new journeys: a_new_scan_accounts_for_its_own_repos_only would say five under the scan-chain alternative the ADR rejected and must say two; a_run_cut_short_after_saving_a_read_of_its_own_keeps_it_for_the_run_after_it builds the one state where a whole-scan count and a last-run count differ with the last run reading strictly less, and asserts the unfinished run shows no count at all. New findings. Owner design: the declared verification command cargo test -p openlore-review-app --lib exits 101, 'no library targets found', so it can never pass; the crafter's --bins substitution is right but undeclared, and the design should say so. Owner implementation: the test-only seam now costs a release build a Mutex lock on the path of every saved read and a new StoreError::Database('scan write seam lock poisoned') branch that no test observes, where the uninhabited fault type already makes refusal impossible, so the seam itself should be cfg-gated; and the recorded mutation miss should be measured against the suite that can kill it, review_app_scan_store_failure, which drives both affected tokens and asserts the run ends interrupted, since as recorded it reads as a surviving mutant in the fault seam when it is an unmeasured one, the declared 80 per cent gate being met at 8 of 9 either way. I did not construct that mutant: it would mean editing candidate production bytes, which this role may not do, so the kill is a reasoned judgement from the cited test bodies. Retained: the two producer-authored proptests outside the recorded oracle, whose remedy this delta now demonstrates, since the acceptance designer recorded two in-crate adapter tests as oracle locators while these two are still in neither list; and Resume still modelling a four-way partition as four parallel collections. Limitations retained: typesafe unavailable, exit 3, key absent from this process, so no service judgment is claimed; this repository has no test-impact selector, so selection stayed mechanical from the touched paths; no timing statement is made, no half-budget or derogation case arose, and the seam finding makes no measured performance claim; native peer messaging exposed no owner session to address, so the findings travel to their owners through the root.
